title.narrative: Strengthening justice and accountability for international crimes in Nigeria

description.narrative: Activities: training workshops (in-person, and online), in-house mentoring sessions, high-level meetings and media engagements.

Outcome 1: Well-trained Nigerian prosecutors who have the knowledge and tools to prosecute international crimes and terrorism under Nigerian law. Outcome 2: Well-trained military investigators and prosecutors of the “Serious Crimes Response Team” (SCRT) equipped with the knowledge and skills to address, under Nigerian law, allegations of war crimes and crimes against humanity committed by the Armed Forces. Outcome 3: Improved and accurate reporting on the investigation and prosecution of international crimes
Prosecutors from the Complex Casework Group within the Directorate of Public Prosecutions, investigators and prosecutors from the Nigerian military and media representatives.

The overall goal of the project is to ensure that the Nigerian justice system is better equipped to investigate and prosecute international crimes genuinely and effectively in line with Nigeria’s obligations under the Rome Statute.
A sum of Euro 66,033 was not spent in the first year due to the covid pandemic. This was spent in the second year of the project.

provider-org.narrative: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands

description.narrative: Project funds from year 2 as well as the left over funds of Euro 66,033 from the first year were spent in the 2nd year of the project.

The final sum of Euro 80,150 is still pending. The final report for the project was submitted in accordance with the contract in January 2022. The final amount will be disbursed after determination of the definite grant by the grantor.

title.narrative: STRENGTHENING JUSTICE AND ACCOUNTABILITY IN NIGERIA

Enhanced Nigerian system of justice that is better equipped to investigate and prosecute international crimes genuinely and effectively in line with Nigeria’s obligations under the Rome Statute and consistent with international law.
Enhanced transparency and communication between the Ministry of Justice (MOJ) and the International Criminal Court with respect to efforts to investigate and prosecute international crimes
Improved and accurate reporting on the investigation and prosecution of international crimes

Investigators and prosecutors of the “Serious Crimes Response Team” have the capacity and the legal expertise to investigate and prosecute, under Nigerian law, international crimes allegedly committed by the Armed Forces
Members of the military have been nominated to the “Serious Crimes Response Team”
Prosecutors of the Complex Casework Group have established a digital workflow to efficiently and effectively build and manage complex cases
Prosecutors of the Complex Casework Group have the knowledge and skills to prosecute international crimes using Nigerian law
Well-trained Nigerian prosecutors who have the knowledge and tools to prosecute international crimes and terrorism under Nigerian law
Well-trained journalists who have the knowledge and skills to report on international crimes

Well-trained military investigators and prosecutors of the “Serious Crimes Response Team” (SCRT) equipped with the knowledge and skills to address, under Nigerian law, allegations of war crimes and crimes against humanity committed by the Armed Forces.
